ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure, there are FU2 fuses at the upper and lower sides respectively, forming the two ends of the control power supply; the upper side passes through SB3 and then splits into left and right two control branches. The left branch has SB1 and a KM1 self-locking contact connected in parallel with it, and below are connected in series a KM2 contact and the KM1 coil; the right branch has SB2 and a KM2 self-locking contact connected in parallel with it, and below are connected in series a KM1 contact and the KM2 coil. The lower ends of the two coils KM1 and KM2 are connected to the same common lower node, and this node is then connected through the FR contact to the lower power line. HL1 and HL2 indicator lamps are also drawn in the figure; they are connected respectively from the middle nodes of the left and right branches to the lower power line. Reasoning: Assume that in the initial state KM1 has already been energized; its coil circuit usually returns to the lower power line through the common lower node and then through FR. When FR operates, the FR contact opens. If it is a standard circuit without bypass, it can be directly considered that the KM1 coil circuit is cut off; but in the partial circuit designed by this student, the common node at the lower ends of the KM1 and KM2 coils is also connected to another coil branch and to the branches from the indicator lamps to the lower power line, so FR opening is not equivalent to completely isolating all possible current paths of the KM1 coil. Therefore, simply analyzing the FR operation as KM1 immediately losing power is incorrect.

method.method_draft: First describe the image structure, then reason from the assumed initial state in which KM1 is energized. Locate the KM1 coil return path through the common lower node and FR. When FR operates, mark the FR contact open and trace whether KM1’s coil is completely isolated. Because the diagram also connects the common coil node to the other coil branch and to indicator-lamp paths to the lower rail, FR opening does not simply remove every possible current path for KM1 in this student-designed partial circuit. Therefore the analysis claiming that FR operation makes KM1 immediately de-energize is the incorrect analysis.
method.CoT_raw: 图像描述：图中上、下方各有FU2熔断器形成控制电源两端；上方经SB3后分成左右两条控制支路。左支路有SB1及与其并联的KM1自锁触点，下面串有KM2触点和KM1线圈；右支路有SB2及与其并联的KM2自锁触点，下面串有KM1触点和KM2线圈。KM1、KM2两个线圈的下端连接到同一个公共下节点，该节点再经FR触点接到下方电源线。图中还画有HL1、HL2指示灯，它们分别从左右支路的中间节点接到下方电源线。推理：假设初始状态下KM1已经得电，其线圈回路通常经公共下节点再通过FR返回下方电源线。当FR动作时，FR触点断开。若是标准且无旁路的回路，可以直接认为KM1线圈回路被切断；但该学生设计的局部电路中，KM1、KM2线圈下端公共节点还与另一线圈支路以及指示灯到下电源线的支路相连，因此FR断开并不等于把KM1线圈的所有可能电流通路都完全隔离。于是，把FR动作简单分析为KM1立即失电是不正确的。

planner_metadata.distinctiveness_rationale: This is the direct circuit-tracing route: it determines the false statement by following actual current paths after FR opens, rather than relying on a generic overload-relay rule.
planner_metadata.image_role: Read the ladder diagram: FU2 supply rails, normally closed SB3 stop contact at the top, left KM1 control branch with SB1 and KM1 self-holding contact plus KM2 interlock contact feeding the KM1 coil, right KM2 branch similarly arranged, indicator lamps HL1/HL2 connected from the coil-side nodes to the lower rail, and the FR contact placed only in the common return below the two contactor coils.
planner_metadata.text_role: Use the question text to know the target is specifically the incorrect analysis about FR’s effect on contactor KM1 in the shown sliding-platform control circuit, not a general description of overload protection.
planner_metadata.knowledge_role: Use ladder-control principles: an overload relay FR normally opens its NC control contact when it operates, but a contactor coil is de-energized immediately only if all return/supply paths for that coil are interrupted. Parallel pilot lamps or the opposite branch can create a residual/bypass path in a misdesigned circuit.
